set.def: being gentle and forgiving, especially in punishing; being less strict than people expect

why: plain-word rule: 'mildness' (zipf 1.8) is rarer than 'leniency' (2.8)
'capture' is a forced opposite (elude = escape; capture is the pursuer's act)
'bane' means a cause of constant trouble, not something hated/unacceptable
'idiom' in this sense is obscure and confusing (learners read it as a set phrase)
'show' conflicts with the def's own 'show that it is untrue'; exude (show a feeling clearly) is a near-opposite of belie for (f)
'slight' is not a real opposite of voluminous
'hanker after' is too rare for learners to recognize
'pithily'/'tersely' too rare; 'wordily' barely in use
'tardily' too rare for learners to recognize
'confidant' is just a spelling variant of the term, a giveaway in (e)
haphazard (without care, messy) is a near-opposite for (f)
stipulate (state clearly) is a near-opposite of allude for (f), whose ant is 'state'
both mean cause to start, near-opposites of forestall (prevent) for (f)
forestall (prevent ahead of time) is a near-opposite for (f)
tactful is a near-opposite of flippant (ant: serious, respectful) for (f)
brusque (rude, blunt) is a near-opposite; tactful's ant includes 'blunt'
garish (showy) is a near-opposite; ant includes 'showy'
staid (serious, dull) is a near-opposite; ant includes 'serious'
leery (careful, fearing danger) is a near-opposite; ant includes 'cautious'
scrupulous (thorough, careful) is a near-opposite; ant includes 'thorough'
berate (attack someone angrily in words) is a near-synonym for (e)
obfuscation (deliberately confusing to hide the truth) overlaps with artifice/deception for (e)
haphazardly (careless, without plan) is a near-opposite for (f)
haphazardly/unceremoniously (careless, rough) are near-opposites; assiduously (with great care) is a near-synonym of carefully
warily (cautiously, watching for danger) is a near-opposite of nonchalantly for (f)
